source.title: On Geometric Understanding and Learned Priors in Feed-forward 3D Reconstruction Models
source.authors: Jelena Bratulić; Sudhanshu Mittal; T. Brox; Christian Rupprecht

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies geometric representations and cross-view correspondence in 3D vision transformers, not induction behavior or in-context learning. It cites the induction-heads work but does not test or use that finding.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on attention-based point correspondence and geometric representation in vision models. These concern a different behavior from induction-head sequence copying; its input-robustness results are not included as findings about induction heads.
record.test_reason: The study probes 3D reconstruction transformers (VGGT, DA3, DUSt3R) for epipolar geometry and cross-view patch correspondence in attention heads. It cites Olsson et al. and Elhage et al. only as general interpretability background. It measures no induction behaviour ([A][B]…[A]→[B]), no in-context learning, and no training dynamics. Cross-view correspondence heads are a related but different construct, not induction heads in another modality. Its 'phase transition' is across layers, not training time, so it does not bear on V2 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that these models encode epipolar structure, strongly indicate use of point correspondences via attention heads, and rely on learned priors. Those priors give robustness to input perturbations but can cause hallucinated correspondences under occlusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses layer-wise probes, QK-attention correspondence measurements, and attention knockouts in 3D vision models; it does not use an induction-head training or measurement procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported layer location differs by architecture: VGGT and DA3 show correspondence and geometric information in middle layers, while DUSt3R shows it in early decoder layers. Knockout impact varies with intervention locality; DUSt3R is especially sensitive to whole-head and image-map interventions.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise probes recover the fundamental matrix from intermediate representations of VGGT, DA3 and DUSt3R. Recovery improves sharply in middle layers for VGGT and DA3, and in early layers for DUSt3R.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction transformers encode epipolar geometry in intermediate layers, with the location depending on architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: QK attention heads match corresponding patches across views, in middle layers for VGGT and DA3 and early decoder layers for DUSt3R. The pattern is consistent across DA3 small, large and giant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some attention heads in multi-view vision transformers implement cross-view point-correspondence matching.

fits_no_version.finding: Knocking out high-correspondence heads greatly increases Sampson error (e.g. +76.9 px for VGGT whole heads). Random early or late layer knockouts have near-zero effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-view correspondence heads causally contribute to geometric encoding in feed-forward 3D reconstruction models.

record.problems: The correspondence-matching experiment uses a ShapeNet test set of 5 scenes. The causal intervention study is on controlled ShapeNet data, and the authors state that knockout effects do not conclusively establish that correspondence matching alone causes geometric encoding. DUSt3R's whole-head and image-map interventions frequently produce invalid predictions; reported results for those cases are restricted to valid predictions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the extraction limit. The paper's input-robustness experiments are not included because they concern 3D reconstruction robustness rather than induction behavior.

untested.parts: Induction heads, previous-token-head composition, and [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying: none measured.
Training-time formation and the loss bump: none measured. The 'phase transition' the paper names is layer-wise, not over training.
In-context learning as loss falling with token index: not measured.
No induction-head detection in any vision model. The correspondence heads are a different behaviour.
No variation of training data or setup.
Few-shot learning mechanisms are not studied.
Formation dynamics over training are not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to 'none'. The DA3 model-size comparison (Appendix C.4) and the robustness experiments are also unrelated to induction heads. Using the word 'phase transition' for a change across layers should not be read as evidence on V2 or V7.

versions.untested_parts: Induction heads, previous-token-head composition, and [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying.
Training-time formation, in-context-learning gains, and training-loss changes.
Induction heads as a mechanism for most in-context learning in large transformers.
Induction behavior across model families, training runs, or modalities.
How training data or setup affects induction-head formation or in-context learning.
Few-shot task learning and its mechanisms.
Whether induction-head formation is one transition or several sub-steps.

rows.subject: VGGT
rows.operation_detail: Train layer-wise two-layer MLP probes to predict the fundamental matrix from camera tokens.
rows.measure: Median Sampson error for fundamental-matrix recovery
rows.value: The paper reports reliable recovery; ability emerges roughly in the middle layers (layers 12–14), with a sudden error improvement and further refinement in final layers.
rows.note: This measures epipolar geometry representation, not induction behavior.

rows.subject: Depth Anything 3 (DA3)
rows.operation_detail: Train layer-wise two-layer MLP probes to predict the fundamental matrix from camera tokens.
rows.measure: Median Sampson error for fundamental-matrix recovery
rows.value: The paper reports reliable recovery; ability emerges roughly in the middle layers (layers 12–14), with a sudden error improvement and further refinement in final layers.
rows.note: The paper says DA3's relevant layers are immediately after global attention is introduced.

rows.subject: DUSt3R
rows.operation_detail: Train layer-wise two-layer MLP probes to predict the fundamental matrix from decoder-block features.
rows.measure: Median Sampson error for fundamental-matrix recovery
rows.value: The paper reports reliable recovery, with the fundamental matrix emerging in early decoder blocks and refining through the layers, with slight divergence in the last layers.
rows.note: This is a different mechanism and task from induction-head sequence copying.

rows.subject: VGGT
rows.operation_detail: Measure whether each source patch's highest QK-attention target matches a ground-truth corresponding patch.

conditions.value: 5 scenes from different object categories; 50 mm focal length; sampling modes averaged across camera-pair configurations

rows.value: Strong correspondence matching is reported across multiple heads in middle layers, roughly layers 10–16; it begins around layer 10 and precedes the fundamental-matrix recovery improvement at layers 13 and 14.
rows.note: This is cross-view spatial correspondence matching, not token-copying induction behavior.

rows.subject: Depth Anything 3 (DA3)
rows.operation_detail: Measure whether each source patch's highest QK-attention target matches a ground-truth corresponding patch.

conditions.value: 5 scenes from different object categories; 50 mm focal length; sampling modes averaged across camera-pair configurations

rows.value: Strong correspondence matching is reported across middle layers of the architecture.
rows.note: The paper reports similar matching trends for DA3 and VGGT.

rows.subject: DUSt3R
rows.operation_detail: Measure whether each source patch's highest QK-attention target matches a ground-truth corresponding patch.

conditions.value: 5 scenes from different object categories; 50 mm focal length; sampling modes averaged across camera-pair configurations

rows.value: Strong correspondence matching is reported from early decoder layers, with performance continuing to improve in middle layers; reverse-direction activity is stronger and uses more active heads.
rows.note: The authors associate the directional asymmetry with DUSt3R's asymmetric cross-attention decoders.

rows.subject: VGGT
rows.operation_detail: Knock out high-correspondence attention heads in selected layers by zeroing attention activations at different locality levels.

conditions.value: High-correspondence heads versus random early or late layers
Whole heads, image map, block, and patch

rows.measure: Change in Sampson error for fundamental-matrix estimates from predicted camera poses
rows.baseline: Random early or late layer interventions have no significant impact.
rows.value: Knocking out high-correspondence middle-layer heads causes significant degradation, described as a complete failure for VGGT at some intervention settings; the degradation trend persists across locality levels.
rows.note: The figure reports locality-specific results, but this row records only the paper's explicit aggregate description.

rows.baseline: Random early or late layer interventions have no significant impact.
rows.value: Interventions in early layers significantly affect performance. Whole-head and image-map interventions frequently produce invalid camera-pose predictions; the paper reports 72% invalid cases for those intervention types.
rows.note: For whole-head and image-map cases, the figure reports results only for valid predictions.

source_check.correct: DUSt3R early-layer interventions significantly affect performance, consistent with early correspondence matching; the blanket negligible early-layer baseline does not apply. Whole-head and image-map results exclude invalid predictions, which constitute 72% of cases. state=cannot_determine for induction_heads.
source_check.problem: The baseline overlooks DUSt3R's early-layer sensitivity; the geometric measure cannot establish an induction-head claim.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2 dated 17 March 2026. Its geometric transition is across network layers, not an induction-head transition during training.

statements.correction: VGGT whole-head intervention: +76.9 pixels median Sampson error. VGGT and DA3: random early/late interventions have no significant impact. DUSt3R: early-layer interventions significantly affect performance; whole-head and image-map results include only valid predictions, excluding 72% invalid cases. Measured construct: cross-view correspondence and epipolar geometry; induction behaviour untested.
statements.problem: The +76.9 px VGGT whole-head result is present, but the near-zero early/late intervention summary omits DUSt3R's significant early-layer sensitivity.
